USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: With Vice Premier Liu He in Washington for the 13th round and the unused Oct. 15 hike of List 3 from 25% to 30% still hanging over the table, the United States should negotiate—explore a sequenced interim path (large ag/energy purchases, lock-in of the IP/tech-transfer text already drafted this year, and a pause or further delay of the Oct. 15 and Dec. 15 tariff steps) without new unilateral commitments. Do not raise tariffs during these talks; do not roll back existing lists or loosen the Huawei Entity List before China puts enforceable text on the table. Reject a China-narrowed agriculture-only mini-deal that drops industrial policy, forced technology transfer, and enforcement.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not existential. After the May collapse and the August–September cascade (List 4A at 15% on ~$110–125B effective Sept. 1; China’s ~$75B retaliation including autos; Huawei Entity List still in force; Treasury manipulator designation), U.S. manufacturing is already paying: ISM fell to 47.8 in September, a 10-year low, with new export orders at 41.0, the weakest since March 2009, and survey comments naming global trade as the main drag. The Fed has cut the funds rate from 2.39% in May to 1.83% in October; the 10-year yield is 1.59% on Oct. 9, down ~96 bp since mid-April—markets are pricing slower growth, not a boom from toughness. Farm-belt exposure remains the clearest political and sectoral hit (soy/pork still under heavy Chinese duties until the mid-September exemption/purchase signal). That maps nearer the +0.5 “material drag / key export sector / domestic pressure” anchor than to opportunity, but it is not +0.5: manufacturing is ~11% of GDP, China has made reciprocal goodwill moves (16-item exemption list Sept. 11; soy/pork excluded from additional tariffs and some cargoes bought after Trump delayed the Oct. 1 hike to Oct. 15), and Washington still holds unused leverage (Oct. 15 rate step, Dec. 15 List 4B on phones/laptops, Entity List). Hence +0.30, not higher and not negative.

Action should stay near zero because further escalation this week would likely meet the countermeasures Chinese state commentary has already previewed and would deepen the factory slump just as talks resume; a unilateral partial rollback or purchase-side concession would spend leverage after Beijing walked back industrial-policy commitments and after the May renegotiation episode. The White House agenda for this round still lists forced tech transfer, IP, services, NTBs, agriculture, and enforcement—so the right stance is to talk, keep existing tariffs and Huawei controls as bargaining chips, and only trade a delay of the next hikes for concrete, sequenced Chinese commitments. That is negotiate, not hold-and-ignore the table and not concede.
key_factors: 13th-round Washington talks (Liu He / Lighthizer / Mnuchin) opening as of the decision date, with China signaling a narrower offer that drops industrial-policy/subsidy reform
Unused U.S. leverage: List 3 25%→30% delayed only to Oct. 15; List 4B (~phones, laptops, toys) still set for Dec. 15; Huawei remains on the Entity List
U.S. manufacturing already contracting: ISM 47.8 in September (lowest since June 2009), export orders 41.0; Fed easing and 10-year yield at 1.59% show growth scare, not tariff-war insulation
Farm-belt retaliation remains the sharpest U.S. political exposure; China’s mid-September soy/pork exemptions and cargoes are goodwill, not a locked purchase commitment
May 2019 collapse after a near-complete text, plus August currency-manipulator designation and rare-earth signaling, argue against trusting an unenforceable mini-deal

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Enter the October 10–11 Washington round prepared to talk, not to punch. Seek a narrow, reversible truce that postpones the October 15 hike of List 3 from 25% to 30% and keeps List 4B off the December 15 calendar, in exchange for limited, already-telegraphed farm purchases and continued technical work on enforcement text. Do not offer structural reform or a large purchase package until the United States puts matching tariff relief on the table, and do not add new tariffs, activate the unreliable-entity list, or tighten rare-earth controls this week.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. By 10 October the United States has already lifted List 3 to 25% (10 May), put Huawei and affiliates on the Entity List (16 May, with 46 more affiliates added 19 August), and imposed List 4A at 15% on roughly $110–125B (1 September). A further 5-point hike on ~$250B is scheduled for 15 October, and List 4B still hangs over 15 December. That combination hits the export machine and a national-champion tech firm at once — the CHN +0.5 anchor (major export sectors, FX pressure, Huawei targeting). August industrial production grew only 4.4% y/y, a 17½-year low; delivered industrial exports fell 4.3% y/y; urban joblessness ticked to 5.3%; the yuan broke 7 and drew a currency-manipulator designation (5 August). Huawei’s first-half revenue was still up 23% and the temporary general license runs to mid-November, so this is not an immediate financial-stability or legitimacy crisis — hence +0.48 rather than +0.7 or +1.0. Action should stay near zero because talks are opening today (Liu He, 13th round, first principal-level meeting on US soil since the May collapse) and both sides have already exchanged small goodwill (China’s 16-item exemption list and soy/pork carve-outs; Trump’s two-week delay of the 1 October hike at Liu’s request). Deputy talks in mid-September produced no new structural text; Beijing’s stated red line remains that any deal must remove US tariffs and be balanced. Escalating now would likely lock in the 15 October hike and harden Entity List policy; conceding purchases or a full rollback before a matching US offer would spend leverage while Liu is not even carrying the “special envoy” title. Negotiate without new commitments is the stance that matches a high-but-manageable threat and a live, low-expectation bargaining window.
key_factors: Pending 15 Oct US hike of List 3 from 25% to 30% on ~$250B, plus List 4B still set for 15 Dec
Huawei remains on the Entity List; 46 additional affiliates added 19 Aug; TGL only to mid-November
China real-economy stress: Aug IP +4.4% y/y (17.5-year low), industrial export deliveries -4.3%, urban unemployment 5.3%, CNY through 7 and manipulator label
13th-round talks opening 10–11 Oct in Washington with low expectations and no special-envoy mandate
Both sides already exchanged limited goodwill (China tariff exemptions / farm carve-outs; US two-week delay of the Oct hike) but remain far apart on tariff removal vs structural demands
